@ · 20 Nov 2026, 23:51 SGT
$NBIS has been getting absolutely crushed lately. But before you panic and sell, understand who is actually running this company.

His name is Arkady Volozh.

In 1989, before the Soviet Union collapsed, Volozh was already developing search technology. In 1997, a year before Google was founded, he co-founded Yandex.

Over the next 25 years, he transformed Yandex into a technology empire worth tens of billions of dollars. He built one of the few search engines in the world capable of beating Google in its home market.

Yandex expanded into cloud computing, AI, autonomous vehicles, e-commerce, and ride-hailing. In 2011, Volozh took the company public on Nasdaq.

Then everything changed in 2022. Following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Volozh was sanctioned by the EU and stepped down from Yandex.

In 2024, Yandex sold its Russian businesses for approximately $5.4 billion. The international businesses remained with the Dutch parent company, which became Nebius Group.

At around 60 years old, when most executives would consider retirement, Volozh decided to build another technology giant.

This time, his focus was AI infrastructure.

Since then, Nebius has secured multibillion-dollar agreements with Microsoft and Meta, attracted investment from NVIDIA, and positioned itself as a major player in the AI infrastructure industry.

Think about that. He built a company capable of challenging Google, lost control of its Russian operations to geopolitics, and started building another multibillion-dollar technology business.

The stock can drop 10%, 20%, or 40%. That doesn’t erase decades of execution.

I’m not bullish on $NBIS because I expect the stock to go up tomorrow.

I’m bullish because I believe Arkady Volozh is building his second technology empire.

And I believe the market is underestimating what he can accomplish.

Inflation in Japan is accelerating:

Japan's CPI inflation excluding fresh food jumped +2.1% YoY in September, its highest YoY increase since December 2025.

Since May, Japan's CPI inflation has risen +0.6 percentage points.

Furthermore, CPI excluding fresh food and energy surged +2.4% YoY, its largest YoY increase since January.

Overall CPI inflation rose +2.1% YoY last month, its highest reading since November 2025.

This comes as the Iran War continues to fuel inflationary pressures in Japan, which relies heavily on imported food and energy.

Meanwhile, Japan's major food and beverage companies planned price increases for 3,153 items in October, the 2nd consecutive monthly reading above 3,000 for the first time since July 2023.

Inflationary pressures in Japan are broadening again.

This metric compares actual economic data with market expectations, rising above 0 when data beats estimates and falling below 0 when data misses expectations.

Excluding July and August 2023, this is the highest reading since the rapid economic recovery following the 2020 Pandemic.

Since August, the index has surged +56 points, or +373%.

Over the last 23 years, the index has exceeded its current level only 5% of the time.

The US economy is gaining momentum.

BREAKING: This past week's -10.4% drop in the Nasdaq 100 was one of the rarest weekly declines in 40 years.

Of the last 2,133 trading weeks, just 11 saw declines of this magnitude or worse.

That's 0.52% of all weeks, a 3.27 standard deviation move based on the historical mean and volatility.

Of course, market returns exhibit "fat tails," meaning extreme moves occur more frequently than a normal distribution would predict.

However, even accounting for the fact that extreme market moves are more common than traditional statistical models suggest, this was a historically rare selloff.

Volatility returns when markets least expect it.

One of the best investing tips I've received is to treat your stock portfolio like an actual business.
Investors should micromanage their positions the same way Jensen micromanaged his subordinates.

Applying to current market conditions, I see absolutely no issues with realising profits/losses in ultra low conviction positions rather than praying to see the H1 highs again.

How do you know which ones these are? Clue - you open your portfolio and think "Why on Earth did I buy this stock, and why the hell do I still own it?"

IMO this type of reflection should be done weekly...but we're here now after a major correction and it's never too late to get started.

Having this type of active reflection each week will fundamentally transform your investing habits.

*Appreciate there's also a "fun" element to all this too, so ask yourself: Am I holding too many 'fun' positions and not enough 'sleep easy' positions?

Investor positioning in copper is cratering:

Speculative investors sold -$1.3 billion in Comex copper futures in the week ending November 10th, marking the 7th consecutive weekly sale.

This group includes hedge funds, commodity trading advisers (CTAs), and other institutional investors.

- Rotate to: utilities, healthcare, staples, bonds
- This is when everyone is comfortable. Nobody is hedging. Nobody is worried. That's exactly when you should be.

For anyone who’s been keeping up with the streams, you know I put a collar on my Nvidia position on Monday before earnings.

This was around $155.

I sold the $165 calls for this week and used that premium to buy the $150 puts. The premium covered 77.5% of the cost and I ended up paying a $0.90 debit for the hedge.

I have just exercised those puts and sold my Nvidia position at $150.

I started buying this name during DeepSeek and ended up getting to an average of $120. Ever since the Jensen news came out, I have felt incredibly uneasy about the position, especially going into earnings given the name couldn’t break out with Jensen on the call so I had no reason to believe it could break out without him.

The risks are simply too high with Nvidia even though the valuation obviously is cheap beyond imagination, assuming the earnings growth continues to be true. The credit backstops, China issues, Jensen not being there…these things could work out but the risk to them at this moment obviously is much higher than normal. The investigation itself is an annoying overhang on the stock regardless of their growth.

I’ve bagheld various names down and stuck with the story, many times with Nvidia in early 2025, but I was not willing to baghold this name because of Jensen’s affairs. I think the majority of retail are in this name between $120-$140 and now basically have to make a decision if they think things will change or if this company continues forward without Jensen.

Nvidia can obviously bounce from here, but it’s less about the price action up. It was cheap at $180 and cheap at $150. I wouldn’t care about buying this back at a higher price than I sold, but there would need to be a reason. Just not interested in this until Jensen comes back, if he does.

What's rather unique about the market correction over the last 45 days is that the market is no longer waiting on President Trump to intervene.

In every major market downturn since January 2025, President Trump has had the ability to intervene and mark a bottom. And, that's almost always what happened.

This includes the trade war, Iran War, Greenland situation, US-China tensions, interest rates, Venezuela, and more.

In our X Article earlier today, we named this financial backstop the "Trump Put."

Minutes ago, President Trump held a press conference and mentioned Iran, Nvidia, China, and Ukraine, but never markets.

With the shift in political power in the US, the era of the "Trump Put" appears to be nearing its end.

The erosion of this backstop for financial markets partially explains why selling pressure has been so strong this week.

This will be a major adjustment for investors.

I covered this earlier in Jan regarding PCB bottlenecks with photonics + $AMZN Kuiper / $SPCX starlink supply chains.

But as an update, it like other industries outside of AI are really starting to feel the pain now too.

Global Electronics Association: "Is issuing this Industry Alert on escalating shortages across the printed circuit board (PCB) supply chain.

Companies in automotive, industrial, medical, defense, and telecommunications report longer lead times and difficulty securing supply as AI absorbs scarce capacity, effectively putting production at risk"

The association meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. The association urged buyers to plan ahead for supply constraints and manufacturers.

Hyperscalers like $AMZN already planned ahead of time taking stakes in Gold Circuit Electronics (2368) for supply procurement...

But can't say the same about other industries procurement (medical industry is probably not used to competing with hyperscalers over the same supply lol).

The resulting shortages of critical materials, including CCLs and fibreglass cloth, are squeezing supplies for consumer electronics.

TLDR: same bottleneck, same timeline for 2028. It's just interesting to see association warnings about it impacting medical to defense industries.

So there's incremental information that it's become an industry wide allocation issue.

I also think it's helpful to see escalating shortages + broadening... so it might show the selloff is starting to look very disconnected with fundamental demand.
